newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa's JSE braces for Q2 listings flood.
newsitem.headline: South Africa's JSE braces for Q2 listings flood.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange, already sporting around 620 company listings, is bracing itself for a slew of flotations in coming months, market analysts said on Thursday.

The JSE, ranked the world's 13th biggest bourse at end-February by number of companies listed, will by the end of this month have seen eight debuts in 1997, just ahead of the seven recorded in the same period last year.
At least another six firms are gearing up to come to the South African market in the next few months with some creating more than a flutter of interest.

Fastfood outlet Nando's Group Holdings, which is to list on Friday, the last flotation this month, announced on Wednesday that its initial public offer to raise 15 million rand had been oversubscribed 24 times, bringing in 361 million rand.
"It is a vote of confidence in our chain and Nando's concept," said firm chairman and founder Robbie Brozin.

After Nando's the JSE, which at February 28 was the 15th biggest equity market ranked by market capitalisation in U.S. dollars, will soon welcome firms active in a wide range of sectors including electronics, mining and horse racing.
"The hot period (for listings) is really May, June, July. The second and third quarters are the most active," Mark Durr, JSE listings director, told Reuters.

"Things seem to always get off to a slow start," he said, attributing this in part to the disruptions of the Christmas holiday and Easter period and to the nine to 13 weeks it takes to organise a new listing.
Electronics firm, Amalgamated Appliances, unbundled from the Malbak Ltd group, will debut on May 8 with a market capitalisation of 95 million rand.
Also early next month is the turn of zinc and copper mining firm Maranda Mining Co which will reverse list into Rooiberg Tin Ltd .
Stantronic, a electronics firm which is to reverse list into the General Technologies Ltd cash shell, is also set for a May appearance.

Other near-term prospects include black empowerment business Molope Bakeries which is expected to go public in May or June; First South Africa Food in June; NHK Investments with two firms, one food, the other property, in the second quarter; and Gauteng province's horse racing industry which said this month it will list "as soon as possible".

A number of companies have stated intentions to join the JSE ranks after June, including newly-merged risk management and insurance broking Glenrand MIB Holdings Ltd. Game reserve group Conservation Corporation Africa has also indicated it is eyeing a listing this year.
Willi Jonker, executive director of portfolio management at Norwich Investments, said new listings were being eyed closely.

"Typically there is a lot of interest and I think that is because fund managers are desperate to find companies that will show earnings growth and the bigger companies we are a bit worried about," Jonker told Reuters.
He said there were concerns that some of the larger firms had enjoyed good growth on high inflation and protection from competition -- factors which had now weakened.

Companies which have emerged on the JSE so far this year are: Celtron Ltd , Stocks Hotels and Resorts Ltd , Megacor Holdings Ltd , Mustek Ltd , Tourism Investment Corp Ltd , Avis Holdings Ltd and Softline Ltd through the Benoni Holdings cash shell, Durr said. Nando's makes up the eight to end-April.
